title: Set B — contradiction: three conflicting founding dates

questions.question: When was the Fernhaven Seed Library founded?
questions.plantedFact: The planted contradiction. harbour-courier-2016 says 'founded in 2014'; carrow-almanac-2021 says it 'began lending seed to the public in early 2015'; charity-register-2020 says 'incorporated as a charitable trust in December 2013'. Three semantically conflicting answers to when the library came into existence, with no shared wording — string matching cannot group them, and a correct run surfaces them side by side as one disputed group rather than averaging or silently picking one.

questions.question: What does the Fernhaven Seed Library do?
questions.plantedFact: All five sources agree it lends seed free of charge and expects borrowers to return saved seed — the profile must not come out all-dispute just because the founding date is contested.

questions.question: Who founded the Fernhaven Seed Library?
questions.plantedFact: Maren Odell — named as founder in the newspaper feature and in the interview's title. The founder is agreed even though the founding date is disputed; a correct run keeps those two questions separate.

questions.question: Where is the Fernhaven Seed Library housed?
questions.plantedFact: Quay Street, Fernhaven — the courier and almanac name the former lifeboat station, the register gives the registered office, and Odell explains why she chose the building.

questions.question: What annual event does the library run?
questions.plantedFact: The Seedling Swap, held in April — described by Odell and reported as the busiest day of the year in the annual report.

questions.question: How many seed varieties does the library hold?
questions.plantedFact: Only the 2019 annual report gives a figure (the catalogue passed six hundred varieties). A single-source question is agreed, not disputed.

questions.question: How is the library staffed?
questions.plantedFact: Only the annual report addresses staffing: run entirely by volunteers, no paid staff.

notes: Planted-contradiction scenario. Exactly one fact is contested — when the library came into existence — and it is planted across three documents in three registers with deliberately disjoint phrasings ('founded in 2014' / 'began lending seed to the public in early 2015' / 'incorporated as a charitable trust in December 2013'), mirroring the canonical example in the project README. Everything else agrees, so a correct run yields exactly one disputed group among six agreed ones. The two documents without a founding date (interview, annual report) exist to check that sources are not dragged into a dispute they never spoke to. Note the corpus is not consistent across sets by design: Set A fixes the founding at 2014, this set contests it.
